chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him: 'A man swears with solemn oaths that he will not buy anything for his family.' He said: 'Let him buy for them, and there is no penalty upon him for his oath.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man swears not to buy things for his family?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the concept of 'al-yamān al-mughallazah' (solemn oath) is clarified as a strong verbal commitment rather than an absolute prohibition, allowing the husband to fulfill his duty of providing for his family without incurring expiation (kaffārah). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that oaths intended to restrict beneficial acts are often interpreted leniently to prevent hardship, distinguishing between the binding nature of the vow and the permissibility of the act itself. The hadith underscores the priority of maintaining family welfare over strict adherence to a self-imposed restriction.
